symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Number of observed system variables.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: Indices of the observed variables.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of nonobservational regimes.

symbols.name: Kcal
symbols.def: Regime indices, with zero denoting observation.

symbols.name: Kplus
symbols.def: Indices of the explicitly nonobservational soft-intervention regimes.

symbols.name: zeta
symbols.def: Exogenous indicator vertex for nonobservational regime \(k\); no intervention-indicator vertex exists at index zero.

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: Generic member of Dai et al.'s causally sufficient model family.

symbols.name: Seta
symbols.def: Binary selection nodes in candidate model \(\eta\).

symbols.name: Geta
symbols.def: Candidate causal DAG before intervention and selection conditioning.

symbols.name: Ieta
symbols.def: Candidate target family with the observational target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\) separated from the unknown nonobservational targets.

symbols.name: Tw
symbols.def: Dai et al.'s selected observational graph at index zero and basal-world interventional twin DAGs only at nonzero indices.

symbols.name: Mproj
symbols.sig: \(\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0))=\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}\) on \(V\), and \(\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k))=\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\) on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\)
symbols.def: Regime-specific MAG projection, with a distinct indicator-free observational branch and indicator-retaining nonobservational branches.

symbols.name: Meq
symbols.def: Two MAGs are related when they have the same adjacencies, unshielded colliders, and collider status on every common discriminating path.

symbols.name: Mfam
symbols.def: Supplied population-oracle MAG representatives: \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) is on \(V\), and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\).

symbols.name: Ccal
symbols.def: All candidate models satisfying the published causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection semantics and whose regime twin MAGs are Markov equivalent to the supplied representatives.

symbols.name: Ecal
symbols.def: Ordered incidence positions \(e=(k,u;uv)\) over the common regime skeletons, one position for each endpoint of each adjacency.

symbols.name: mark
symbols.def: Tail or arrowhead at endpoint position \(e\) in a fully oriented MAG.

symbols.name: PSI
symbols.def: Canonical SI-PAG family whose endpoint marks are the marks invariant over \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), with a circle at every noninvariant endpoint.

symbols.name: Pinit
symbols.def: The matrix-encoded family obtained by orienting unshielded colliders in every regime and intervention-indicator tails only in regimes indexed by \(\mathcal K_+\); all further within- and cross-regime orientations are delegated to \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\).

symbols.name: Hext
symbols.def: Technique handle combining discriminating-path closure, twin-graph descendant and ancestral-selection labels, and realizability-preserving paired completions.

symbols.name: RSI
symbols.def: Finite rule system to be derived by \(\texttt{oeq:si-extension-calculus}\), containing ordinary within-regime FCI rules and twin-compatible cross-regime rules from handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{ext}}\).

symbols.name: Cl
symbols.def: Least fixed point obtained by repeatedly replacing a circle endpoint by a tail or arrowhead using a rule in \(\mathsf R\), never deleting an adjacency or reversing a fixed mark.

symbols.name: Nend
symbols.def: Maximum number of endpoint positions over one observational graph on \(D\) vertices and \(K\) intervention graphs on \(D+1\) vertices.

symbols.name: Lin
symbols.def: Number of entries in one \(D\)-vertex observational adjacency-mark matrix and \(K\) nonobservational \(D+1\)-vertex adjacency-mark matrices.

symbols.name: arule
symbols.def: Number of regime placeholders in the finite code of rule \(r\).

symbols.name: brule
symbols.def: Number of vertex placeholders in the finite code of rule \(r\).

symbols.name: Trule
symbols.def: Worst-case time for one exhaustive match scan of finitely coded rule \(r\), including cubic-time graph searches for its path premises.

symbols.name: Tclose
symbols.def: Total time to materialize the initial family and run successful rule scans plus the final no-update scan on the encoded oracle MAG family.

symbols.name: Rcert
symbols.def: Finite certificate in which the supplied observational skeleton and indicator-neighborhoods determine both the residual co-selection two-section and every normalized target set after choosing the basal DAG and ancestor-closed selected set.

symbols.name: CheckDai
symbols.type: finite input-conditioned target-residual Dai certificate checker
symbols.def: Accepts exactly when the target-residual certificate-generated regime MAG family matches the supplied adjacency and unshielded-collider patterns.

symbols.name: CDIScmp
symbols.type: enumerative population graphical algorithm over target-residual certificates
symbols.def: Enumerates only basal graphs and ancestor-closed selected sets; derives the unique co-selection and target residuals; and returns endpointwise feasible-mark invariance with opposing accepted certificates for every circle.

assumptions.condition: For candidate \(\eta\), \(\mathcal G_\eta\) is a finite directed acyclic graph on \(V\cup S_\eta\).
Candidate \(\eta\) contains no latent common cause of two vertices in \(V\).

standard.name: Dai et al. binary selection-node convention

assumptions.condition: Every vertex in \(S_\eta\) has no child in \(\mathcal G_\eta\).

standard.name: Dai et al. childless selection nodes

assumptions.condition: Every parent in \(\mathcal G_\eta\) of a vertex in \(S_\eta\) belongs to \(V\).

standard.name: Dai et al. observed-parent selection nodes

assumptions.condition: The observed stratum for candidate \(\eta\) conditions on \(S_\eta=\mathbf 1\).
The conditioned selection-node set in \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) and in \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) equals the basal copy \(S_\eta^*\).
The observational regime has empty intervention target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\).
For each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), every structural mechanism outside \(I_\eta^{(k)}\) and its exogenous input are shared with the basal world.
The indicator-free observational projection \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}\) on \(V\) is Markov equivalent to the supplied observational representative \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\).
For every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the projected twin MAG \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\) on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) is Markov equivalent to the supplied nonobservational representative \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\).
The supplied family has at least one compatible model: \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Separated observational and interventional twin graphs
definitions.construction: Define \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) as the indicator-free selected observational DAG on reality vertices \(X_V\) and basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\): copy \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) onto \(X_V\), copy each selection-parent edge into \(S_\eta^*\), and introduce no basal system copy, shared-noise vertex, or intervention-indicator vertex. Separately, for each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), form \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) on reality vertices \(X_V\), basal copies \(X_i^*\) and shared noises \(\varepsilon_i\) for \(i\in\operatorname{de}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(I_\eta^{(k)})\), basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\), and \(\zeta_k\). Copy each edge of \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) into each available world, route unaffected parents into affected basal children, copy selection-parent edges only into \(S_\eta^*\), add \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i^*\), and add \(\zeta_k\to X_i\) exactly for \(i\in I_\eta^{(k)}\).

definitions.name: Regime MAG projection
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0);X_V,\varnothing,S_\eta^*)\), retaining exactly \(V\) and no intervention indicator. Separately, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k);X_V\cup\{\zeta_k\},X^*\cup\varepsilon,S_\eta^*)\). In either branch, join two retained vertices exactly when an inducing path exists after the stated marginalization and conditioning, then place a tail at an endpoint exactly when that endpoint is an ancestor of the other endpoint or of \(S_\eta^*\), and an arrowhead otherwise.

definitions.name: Regime endpoint domain
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E(\mathbf M)=\{(k,u;uv):k\in\mathcal K,\ uv\in E(\mathcal M^{(k)}),\ u\in\{u,v\}\}\).

definitions.name: Canonical SI-PAG
definitions.construction: For each \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), set \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=a\in\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}\) when \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)})=a\) for every \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), and set \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\circ\) otherwise; retain the common regime skeletons.

definitions.name: Initial regime family
definitions.construction: On the observational skeleton on \(V\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders. On each nonobservational skeleton indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders and every endpoint at the existing indicator \(\zeta_k\) as a tail. No indicator endpoint is introduced in regime zero. Store the resulting family as adjacency and endpoint-mark matrices \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\); ordinary FCI closure and cross-regime propagation are both performed by \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\).

definitions.name: Twin-compatible extension handle
definitions.construction: Handle: start from the ordinary discriminating-path and uncovered-path closure inside each regime; attach the descendant and ancestral-selection labels forced by Dai et al.'s twin-MAG lemmas; propagate only label consequences shared across regimes; then adapt Jaber et al.'s I-MAG realizability lemma and Zhang's circle-component completion to construct, for a chosen unresolved endpoint, one tail completion and one arrowhead completion that are projections of a single common basal DAG with one ordered unknown-target family.

definitions.name: Finite oracle-MAG encoding
definitions.construction: Encode \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) by one \(D\times D\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\), and encode each \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\), \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), by one \((D+1)\times(D+1)\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The representation length is \(L_{\mathrm{in}}=D^2+K(D+1)^2\), and regime zero has no row or column for an indicator.

definitions.name: Finite SI-rule encoding and matcher
definitions.construction: Encode each \(r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) by a finite tuple of \(a_r\) typed regime placeholders, \(b_r\) typed vertex placeholders, adjacency and endpoint-mark premises, finite-state uncovered-path or discriminating-path predicates, and a nonempty list of circle-to-tail or circle-to-arrow updates. Regime placeholders are typed as either \(\{0\}\) or \(\mathcal K_+\), and an indicator term may occur only with the latter type. Match \(r\) by enumerating its regime and vertex assignments and deciding every path predicate by breadth-first search on its finite product-state graph. One exhaustive scan has cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\).

definitions.name: Monotone rule closure
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R}(\mathcal P)=\bigvee_{t\ge0}\mathsf R^t(\mathcal P)\), where the join is taken in the endpoint information order \(\circ\prec\mathrm{tail}\) and \(\circ\prec\mathrm{arrow}\), and every strict step fixes at least one previously circular endpoint.

definitions.name: Oracle-input closure schedule
definitions.construction: Materialize \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\) from the encoded oracle family by enumerating triples, then scan the finitely encoded rules in a fixed order and apply every consistent match found in a scan. Repeat after each scan that makes at least one strict endpoint update and stop after the first no-update scan. Record the certificate consisting of the ordered strict updates and the terminal no-match result. Its runtime envelope is \(T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)=O((K+1)(D+1)^3+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K))\).

definitions.name: Input-conditioned normalized target-residual Dai certificate
definitions.construction:
Given the encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), write \(S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)})\).  For every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), define the supplied indicator-neighborhood and its decomposition at \(A\) by
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M)=\{j\in V:\zeta_k\text{ is adjacent to }j\text{ in }\mathcal M^{(k)}\},
\qquad
R_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\cap A,
\qquad
O_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\setminus A.
\]
For a directed acyclic graph \(E\) on \(V\) and \(A\subseteq V\), define
\[
B(E,A)=\left\{\{i,j\}\in\binom V2:
i\to j\in E\ \text{or}\ j\to i\in E\ \text{or}\
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\ \text{in }E
\right\},
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A).
\]
Call \((E,A)\) residual-admissible when
\[
\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A,
\qquad
B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M),
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\subseteq\binom A2,
\]
and, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in the induced DAG \(E[A]\), equivalently
\[
r\in R_k(\mathbf M,A)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{de}_E(r)\cap A\subseteq R_k(\mathbf M,A).
\]
For a residual-admissible pair, set
\[
\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)=
\left\{r\in R_k:
\bigl(\operatorname{an}_E(r)\setminus\{r\}\bigr)\cap R_k=\varnothing
\right\},
\]
\[
T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=O_k(\mathbf M,A)\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k(\mathbf M,A)),
\qquad
F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E\!\left(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\right).
\]
The input-conditioned normalized target-residual Dai certificate is the uniquely derived tuple
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Neither \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) nor any target set is independently enumerated.  When \(K=0\), the tuple has no nonobservational coordinate and no objects \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T^*_{k,\mathbf M},F^*_{k,\mathbf M}\) are introduced; set only the observational target to \(T_0^*=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Complete population target-residual certificate CDIS
definitions.construction:
Enumerate in a fixed lexicographic order only pairs \((E,A)\), where every unordered vertex pair has one of the three basal states absent, oriented one way, or oriented the other way, and \(A\subseteq V\).  For each pair derive \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) and, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), derive \(Z_k(\mathbf M)\), \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\), \(O_k(\mathbf M,A)\), \(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\), and \(F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) as in \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  Reject the pair unless \(E\) is acyclic, \(A\) is ancestor-closed, the residual-skeleton conditions hold, and every \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in \(E[A]\).  For each survivor form the unique target-residual certificate
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right)
\]
and retain it precisely when \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\).  Neither the co-selection residual nor any target set is independently enumerated.  If no certificate passes, return \(\mathsf{incompatible}\).  Otherwise, for every \(e=(k,u;uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), form
\[
B_e(\mathbf M)=\left\{\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\bigr):
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\right\}
\subseteq\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]
Set the output mark at \(e\) to the unique element when \(B_e(\mathbf M)\) is a singleton and to a circle when it contains both marks.  For every circle, retain the first accepted tail certificate and the first accepted arrowhead certificate.  Define \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)\) to be this partial-graph family together with those coupled certificates.  Its observational component is on \(V\), and only a component indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  When \(K=0\), enumerate only \((E,A)\), construct only the observational component, and introduce no nonobservational target-residual objects.

definitions.name: Finite input-conditioned target-residual Dai checker
definitions.construction:
Given \(\mathbf M\), enumerate a pair \((E,A)\) and reject it unless it is residual-admissible under \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  For a survivor derive, rather than enumerate,
\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
F_k^*=F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)
\quad(k\in\mathcal K_+),
\]
and set
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q,(T_k^*)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})=(\mathcal N^{(0)},\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)})\) as follows.  The observational graph has vertex set \(V\); distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\{i,j\}\in Q.
\]
Its adjacency set is \(B(E,A)\cup Q=S_0(\mathbf M)\).  At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A\) and every internal vertex belongs to \(F_k^*\).  The indicator \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)=Z_k(\mathbf M),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the exhaustive cases
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k^*&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin F_k^*\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k^*,\ j\notin F_k^*\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same unshielded collider triples; otherwise set it to zero.  All tests and all derived sets are finite matrix computations.  If \(K=0\), construct and compare only the indicator-free observational graph and introduce no \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T_k^*\), or \(F_k^*\).

statements.statement: For any finite \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) represented by \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\) and monotone in the endpoint information order, the schedule in \(\texttt{def:closure-runtime-certificate}\) terminates after at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}=D(D-1)+KD(D+1)\) strict endpoint updates and one terminal no-update scan. Rule \(r\) is matched in \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\) time, and the total oracle-input orientation runtime is \(T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)=O((K+1)(D+1)^3+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K))\), which is polynomial in the finite input dimensions because the rule set and every \(a_r,b_r\) are fixed independently of \(D,K\).
statements.justification: The per-rule matcher and endpoint potential turn finite closure into a checkable total runtime certificate on the supplied oracle graphs.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention gives iterative CDIS pseudocode but no finite rule encoding, per-rule matching cost, or oracle-input closure runtime.
statements.consumer: A population implementation can audit every orientation scan and certify polynomial mark propagation without a complexity claim for discovering the oracle MAGs.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The observational matrix has at most \(D(D-1)\) ordered endpoint positions, and the \(K\) nonobservational matrices have at most \(KD(D+1)\) such positions.  Hence the total number of positions at which a circle can be replaced is at most
\[
N_{\mathrm{end}}=D(D-1)+KD(D+1).
\]
By the monotonicity hypothesis and \(\texttt{def:monotone-closure}\), a strict update replaces at least one circle by a tail or an arrowhead, and no later update can erase or reverse that mark.  Thus the endpoint potential, defined as the number of circular positions, decreases by at least one at every strict update and is initially at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\).  There are consequently at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) strict endpoint updates, at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) scans that make an update, and exactly one final scan that certifies that no rule matches consistently.

For a fixed rule \(r\), \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\) enumerates at most \((K+1)^{a_r}\) assignments of its typed regime placeholders and at most \((D+1)^{b_r}\) assignments of its vertex placeholders.  Its finite-state path predicates are decided on product-state graphs of size polynomial in \(D+1\); the stipulated cubic envelope gives
\[
T_r(D,K)=O\!\left((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3}\right).
\]
Materializing the initial family by enumerating triples costs \(O((K+1)(D+1)^3)\).  Summing one exhaustive match scan for every rule over at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) successful scans and the terminal unsuccessful scan yields
\[
T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)
=O\!\left((K+1)(D+1)^3
+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K)\right).
\]
The rule list and the integers \(a_r,b_r\) are fixed independently of \(D,K\), so the displayed expression is polynomial in \(D,K\), hence also in the finite matrix-input dimensions.  This argument is conditional on the separately supplied finite monotone rule list; it asserts no semantic completeness property and uses no conditional-independence discovery bound. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{ext}}\), can one construct a finite within- and cross-regime rule system \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D,K\), such that every rule has the typed finite representation in \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\), has per-scan cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\), and is sound over \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\); and such that for every endpoint \(e\) left circular by \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M))\) there exist \(\eta_e^{\mathrm t},\eta_e^{\mathrm a}\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) whose indicator-free observational projection and indicator-bearing nonobservational projections agree with every fixed closure mark while realizing respectively a tail and an arrowhead at \(e\)?
statements.justification: The paired global extension is the first proof step not supplied by ordinary FCI, unknown-intervention FCI, or Dai's soundness argument.
statements.gap: Zhang2008CompleteFCI constructs witnesses for one MAG class and JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020 realizes one augmented I-MAG; neither preserves a common basal selected DAG and all unknown-target regimes simultaneously.
statements.consumer: Residual circles in the sciPlex2 A549 analysis become certified nonidentifiabilities rather than artifacts of an incomplete orientation list.

statements.statement:
For every compatible encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), the target-residual certificate algorithm satisfies \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\), is population sound and complete, and returns actual paired compatible certificates for every residual circle.  It checks at most \(3^{\binom D2}2^D\) pairs \((E,A)\), deriving both \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) and every \(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) from the supplied oracle MAGs, with crude runtime
\[
O\!\left(3^{\binom D2}2^D
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
This is a non-tight singly exponential upper bound in \(D^2\), with \(K\) appearing only polynomially, and is not a polynomial overall bound.  The observational output is on \(V\), each nonobservational certificate component is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), and the case \(K=0\) contains no indicator or target-residual objects.  No polynomial claim is made for the conditional-independence and invariance queries needed to obtain \(\mathbf M\), and no completeness assertion is made for a fixed polynomial local CDIS calculus.
statements.justification: The headline combines exact target-residual common realizability with a singly exponential search in \(D^2\) and polynomial regime dependence.
statements.gap: Dai et al. prove local-rule soundness but not complete recovery of the endpoint-invariance SI-PAG.
statements.consumer: Population benchmarking on supplied sciPlex2 A549 regime MAGs obtains the exact target graph and globally compatible opposing certificates.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The matrix family in \(\texttt{def:oracle-input-encoding}\) is exactly the input consumed by \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\).  Applying \(\texttt{thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M),
\]
the candidate bound \(3^{\binom D2}2^D\), and the runtime bound
\[
O\!\left(3^{\binom D2}2^D
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
The endpointwise feasible-mark identity proved there establishes population soundness because every fixed output mark occurs in every compatible member.  It establishes population completeness because every invariant mark is fixed, while every residual circle is accompanied by accepted tail and arrowhead certificates.  By \(\texttt{thm:finite-common-realizability}\), those certificates reconstruct actual members of the full Dai compatibility class and are globally coherent across all regimes.

The domain statement follows from the two branches of \(\texttt{def:dai-certificate-checker}\): \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\) is on \(V\) and contains no intervention indicator, while \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) only for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\).  When \(K=0\), this latter branch is absent.  Moreover,
\[
\log\!\left(3^{\binom D2}2^D\right)=O(D^2),
\]
so the search is singly exponential in \(D^2\), while \(K\) occurs only in the polynomial per-candidate factor.  The procedure starts from supplied oracle MAG matrices; its correctness and runtime exclude their discovery by conditional-independence or invariance queries.  No step invokes a complete fixed local calculus, which remains the separate open-ended question.  No numerical overlap, rank, inverse, division, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For Dai et al.'s two-variable regime family with \(K=1\) and intervention on the first variable, the selected collider model \(1\to S\leftarrow2\) and the unselected directed model \(2\to1\) belong to the same \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\). Consequently, the canonical observational edge has a circle at the endpoint of vertex \(1\) and a tail at the endpoint of vertex \(2\); no sound SI-PAG calculus may orient the first endpoint.
statements.justification: The smallest published equivalence witness fixes a nontrivial boundary that the completeness theorem must preserve.

statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Proof.}
\emph{Construction of the boundary instance.}
Set \(D=2\), \(V=\{1,2\}\), and \(K=1\).  Consider
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{sel}}
 =\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{sel}},\{S\},(\varnothing,\{1\})\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{sel}}:\ 1\longrightarrow S\longleftarrow2,
\]
where \(S\) is binary and the observed stratum is \(S=1\), and
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{dir}}
 =\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{dir}},\varnothing,(\varnothing,\{1\})\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{dir}}:\ 2\longrightarrow1.
\]
These are the two candidates in the clinical two-variable witness of
\cite{DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention}.  Define the supplied oracle representatives by
\[
 \mathcal M^{(0)}:\ X_1\mathbin{---}X_2,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M^{(1)}:\
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2,
 \qquad
 \mathbf M=(\mathcal M^{(0)},\mathcal M^{(1)}).
 \tag{1}
\]
In accordance with the boundary convention in \(\texttt{def:twin-graph}\), the
observational representative has no intervention-indicator vertex.

Both basal graphs are finite DAGs and neither has a latent common cause of the two
system vertices.  In \(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\), the unique selection node is binary,
childless, and has only observed parents; for \(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), the corresponding
selection conditions are vacuous.  The observational target is empty and the sole
nonobservational target is \(\{1\}\) in both candidates.  Selection is imposed on the
basal copy, and the intervention changes only the mechanism of \(X_1\), while all
other mechanisms and exogenous inputs are shared.  Thus the structural member
conditions in \(\texttt{def:dai-compatible-class}\) hold.  It remains to calculate the
two regime projections.

For \(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\), the indicator-free observational graph is
\[
 X_1\longrightarrow S^*\longleftarrow X_2.
\]
After conditioning on \(S^*\), the displayed path induces an adjacency between the
two retained vertices.  Each endpoint is an ancestor of \(S^*\); hence the endpoint
rule in \(\texttt{def:mag-projection}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}}^{(0)}:
 X_1\mathbin{---}X_2.
 \tag{2}
\]
For target \(\{1\}\), the nonobservational twin graph has the relevant edges
\[
 \zeta_1\to X_1,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_1\to X_1,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_1\to X_1^*,
 \qquad
 X_1^*\to S^*,
 \qquad
 X_2\to S^*.
 \tag{3}
\]
Marginalizing \(X_1^*,\varepsilon_1\) and conditioning on \(S^*\), the path
\[
 X_1\leftarrow\varepsilon_1\to X_1^*\to S^*\leftarrow X_2
\]
induces \(X_2\to X_1\): its endpoint at \(X_2\) is a tail because \(X_2\) is an
ancestor of \(S^*\), and its endpoint at \(X_1\) is an arrowhead because \(X_1\) is
an ancestor of neither \(X_2\) nor \(S^*\).  The direct edge
\(\zeta_1\to X_1\) is retained.  There is no inducing path between \(\zeta_1\) and
\(X_2\): the only graph path between them contains the retained nonendpoint
\(X_1\) as the collider \(\zeta_1\to X_1\leftarrow\varepsilon_1\), and \(X_1\)
has no descendant in \(\{X_2\}\cup\{S^*\}\).  Consequently,
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}}^{(1)}:
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2.
 \tag{4}
\]

For \(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), there is neither marginalization nor conditioning in the
observational branch, so
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}}^{(0)}:
 X_2\longrightarrow X_1.
 \tag{5}
\]
In the target-\(1\) twin graph, the reality-world edges
\(\zeta_1\to X_1\) and \(X_2\to X_1\) are retained.  Every graph path from
\(\zeta_1\) to \(X_2\) contains the retained collider \(X_1\) as a nonendpoint,
and there is no selected vertex to activate that collider.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}}^{(1)}:
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2.
 \tag{6}
\]
The two observational MAGs in (2) and (5) are Markov equivalent: each has the
single adjacency \(X_1-X_2\), and a two-vertex graph has no unshielded triple or
discriminating path.  The two nonobservational MAGs in (4) and (6) are identical.
Thus both equivalence-match conditions hold, and therefore
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{sel}},\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}
 \in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M).
 \tag{7}
\]

\emph{Invariance of the endpoint at vertex \(2\).}
The pair in (7) alone shows noninvariance at vertex \(1\); to establish the claimed
tail at vertex \(2\), fix an arbitrary
\(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Observational equivalence to
\(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) gives the adjacency \(X_1-X_2\).  Interventional equivalence to
\(\mathcal M^{(1)}\) gives exactly the skeleton
\[
 \zeta_1-X_1-X_2,
 \qquad
 \zeta_1\not\sim X_2,
 \tag{8}
\]
and makes the unshielded triple in (8) a collider at \(X_1\).

Suppose for contradiction that the observational mark at the endpoint of \(X_2\)
were an arrowhead.  The observational projection retains both system vertices,
marginalizes no system or exogenous vertex, and conditions only on childless selection
sinks.  Since \(D=2\), a nondirect path between \(X_1\) and \(X_2\) can have only
selection vertices as nonendpoints.  Any such adjacency-producing path passes through
a selected common child, making both endpoints ancestors of the conditioned set and
therefore giving tails at both endpoints.  A bidirected edge cannot arise because causal
sufficiency excludes a latent common cause of \(X_1\) and \(X_2\).  The assumed
arrowhead at \(X_2\) must therefore come from the basal causal edge
\[
 1\longrightarrow2.
 \tag{9}
\]

Next, (8) determines the intervention target.  If
\(2\in I_\eta^{(1)}\), then \(\texttt{def:twin-graph}\) inserts the direct retained
edge \(\zeta_1\to X_2\), contradicting \(\zeta_1\not\sim X_2\).  If
\(I_\eta^{(1)}=\varnothing\), the exogenous indicator \(\zeta_1\) has no incident
edge at all, contradicting \(\zeta_1\sim X_1\).  As \(V=\{1,2\}\), these two
facts imply
\[
 I_\eta^{(1)}=\{1\}.
 \tag{10}
\]
By (9)--(10), the nonobservational twin graph contains the retained reality-world
edge \(X_1\to X_2\).  Thus \(X_1\) is an ancestor of \(X_2\), and the endpoint
rule of \(\texttt{def:mag-projection}\) puts a tail at \(X_1\) on their
interventional MAG edge.  This contradicts the arrowhead at \(X_1\) required by the
unshielded collider in (8).  Therefore the supposition was false, and
\[
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,2;12)}(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)})
 =\mathrm{tail}
 \quad\text{for every }\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M).
 \tag{11}
\]

\emph{Canonical marks and the soundness boundary.}
Equation (2) supplies a tail at the observational endpoint of \(X_1\), whereas
(5) supplies an arrowhead there.  By (7), both are compatible witnesses, so the
definition of the canonical SI-PAG gives a circle at that endpoint.  Equation (11)
and the same definition give a tail at the endpoint of \(X_2\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,1;12)}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\circ,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,2;12)}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\mathrm{tail}.
 \tag{12}
\]
A sound SI-PAG calculus may fix an endpoint only to a mark shared by every member
of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Fixing the first endpoint to a tail is refuted by
\(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), while fixing it to an arrowhead is refuted by
\(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\).  Thus no sound calculus may orient that endpoint.

This is a finite graphical boundary result.  No distributional support, positivity,
overlap, rank, division, inverse, or limiting condition is used.  The operative boundary
conditions are \(D=2\), \(K=1\), an indicator-free observational branch, and one
indicator-bearing intervention on vertex \(1\); nonemptiness of the compatibility class
is witnessed explicitly by (7).  \(\square\)

Let \((E,A)\) be residual-admissible for \(\mathbf M\), and let \(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) be its input-conditioned normalized target-residual Dai certificate.  The pair-node and \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\)-isolated singleton-node reconstruction has selection-parent union and ancestor closure exactly \(A\) and two-section exactly \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\).  For each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), descendant closure of \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) and ancestor closure of \(A\) imply
\[
F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\cap A=R_k(\mathbf M,A),
\qquad
T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\cup\bigl(F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\cap A\bigr)=Z_k(\mathbf M).
\]
In the causally sufficient, childless-selection, pre-treatment twin construction, Dai et al.'s MAG formulas give exactly the observational adjacencies, interventional path-induced adjacencies, indicator adjacencies, and endpoint orientations used to construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\) in \(\texttt{def:dai-certificate-checker}\).  Moreover, two such common-basal and ordered-target families are Markov equivalent across all regimes if and only if their corresponding regime MAGs have the same adjacencies and unshielded collider triples in every regime.  If \(K=0\), only the observational clauses apply.

statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix a residual-admissible pair \((E,A)\), abbreviate
\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\quad R_k=R_k(\mathbf M,A),
\quad O_k=O_k(\mathbf M,A),
\quad T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),
\quad F_k^*=F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A).
\]
The residual conditions give \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\), \(B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M)\), and \(Q\subseteq\binom A2\).

Construct one binary childless selection node with parent set \(\{i,j\}\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in Q\), and one with singleton parent set \(\{i\}\) for every \(i\in A\) isolated in \(Q\).  Since \(Q\subseteq\binom A2\), all reconstructed parents lie in \(A\).  Every nonisolated vertex of \(A\) occurs in a pair parent set and every isolated vertex occurs in its singleton parent set.  Hence the union of selection-parent sets is \(A\), its ancestor closure is \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\), and the two-section is exactly \(Q\), including \(A=\varnothing\) and \(Q=\varnothing\).

Because \(R_k\) is descendant-closed in the finite DAG \(E[A]\), every \(r\in R_k\) descends from some \(m\in\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\): repeatedly choose a strict ancestor in \(R_k\), which must terminate by finiteness and acyclicity.  Conversely, descendant closure keeps every descendant in \(A\) of such an \(m\) inside \(R_k\).  Thus
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))\cap A=R_k.
\]
Since \(O_k\subseteq V\setminus A\) and \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\), no vertex of \(O_k\) has a descendant in \(A\).  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(O_k)\cap A=\varnothing,
\qquad
F_k^*\cap A
=\operatorname{de}_E(O_k\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))\cap A
=R_k.
\]
Since \(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\subseteq R_k\),
\[
T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)
=O_k\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\cup R_k
=O_k\cup R_k
=Z_k(\mathbf M).
\]

We now match \(\texttt{def:dai-certificate-checker}\) to \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-substrate}\).  An observational adjacency is generated by a basal edge, by a common observed collider child in \(A\), or by a common selection child.  The first two clauses form \(B(E,A)\), and the third is membership in \(Q\).  Hence
\[
B(E,A)\cup Q
=B(E,A)\cup(S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A))
=S_0(\mathbf M).
\]
The substrate's observational endpoint criterion is exactly that the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the substrate's intervention-induced adjacency is exactly a path in the observational graph whose vertices lie in \(A\) and whose internal vertices lie in \(F_k^*\).  Its indicator adjacency set is \(T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\), with every such edge \(\zeta_k\to j\).  After preserving an observational directed orientation, its four exhaustive endpoint cases depend only on membership in \(F_k^*\) and ancestry in \(E\), exactly as in the checker.  Thus \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\) is the regime-MAG family given by Dai et al.'s formulas for the reconstruction.

Finally, the cross-regime clause of \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-substrate}\) says that two common-basal, ordered-target families are Markov equivalent in all regimes exactly when their regime MAGs have equal adjacency and unshielded-collider patterns.  This is precisely the terminal checker comparison.  If \(K=0\), \(\mathcal K_+\) is empty, so only the observational argument remains.  No support, overlap, rank, inverse, division, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

For every \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), let \(E=\mathcal G_\eta[V]\), let
\[
A=\operatorname{an}_E\!\left(\bigcup_{s\in S_\eta}\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(s)\right),
\]
and let \(Q_\eta\) contain \(\{i,j\}\) exactly when some \(s\in S_\eta\) has \(\{i,j\}\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(s)\).  Then
\[
B(E,A)\cup Q_\eta=S_0(\mathbf M),
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A)\subseteq Q_\eta.
\]
For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), put \(T_k=I_\eta^{(k)}\) and \(F_k=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)\).  The supplied indicator-neighborhood satisfies
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M)=T_k\cup(F_k\cap A),
\qquad
T_k\setminus A=O_k(\mathbf M,A),
\qquad
F_k\cap A=R_k(\mathbf M,A),
\]
the set \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in \(E[A]\), and the derived target residual obeys
\[
\operatorname{de}_E\!\left(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\right)=F_k.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) is an input-conditioned normalized target-residual certificate.  Replacing the selection nodes by the pair-node and isolated-singleton reconstruction and replacing every nonobservational target by \(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) produces \(\bar\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) with exactly the same projected MAG in every regime.  Conversely, every normalized target-residual certificate is the exact \((A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\) selection summary with the uniquely derived target family of this reconstruction, which uses at most \(\binom D2+D\) selection nodes.  When \(K=0\), there are no target-residual objects or target replacements.
statements.justification: The exact quotient removes both independent co-selection choices and redundant target choices while preserving every regime MAG in the full class.

statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), and put
\[
E=\mathcal G_\eta[V],
\qquad
U_\eta=\bigcup_{s\in S_\eta}\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(s),
\qquad
A=\operatorname{an}_E(U_\eta).
\]
By \(\operatorname{ass{:}selection\text{-}parents}\), \(U_\eta\subseteq V\).  Hence \(A\subseteq V\), and idempotence of ancestor closure gives \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\).  The restriction \(E\) of the finite DAG \(\mathcal G_\eta\) is acyclic.  If \(\{i,j\}\in Q_\eta\), then \(i,j\in U_\eta\subseteq A\), so \(Q_\eta\subseteq\binom A2\).

By the observational formula in \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-checker-characterization}\), the observational projection of \(\eta\) has adjacency set \(B(E,A)\cup Q_\eta\).  Membership in \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) entails observational Markov equivalence to \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\), and Markov-equivalent MAGs have the same adjacencies.  Therefore
\[
B(E,A)\cup Q_\eta=S_0(\mathbf M).
\]
It follows that
\[
B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M),
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)
=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A)
\subseteq Q_\eta
\subseteq\binom A2.
\]

Fix \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), write \(T_k=I_\eta^{(k)}\), and let \(F_k=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)\).  The indicator formula in \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-checker-characterization}\) and compatibility give
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M)=T_k\cup(F_k\cap A).
\]
Because \(F_k\cap A\subseteq A\), taking the difference with \(A\) gives
\[
O_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\setminus A=T_k\setminus A.
\]
Since \(T_k\subseteq F_k\), intersecting the indicator identity with \(A\) gives
\[
R_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\cap A=F_k\cap A.
\]
If \(r\in R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) and \(a\in\operatorname{de}_E(r)\cap A\), transitivity of descendants gives \(a\in F_k\cap A=R_k(\mathbf M,A)\).  Thus \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in \(E[A]\).

Write \(R_k=R_k(\mathbf M,A)\), \(O_k=O_k(\mathbf M,A)\), and \(T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\).  Since \(A\) is ancestor-closed, no vertex outside \(A\) has a descendant in \(A\), and so
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(O_k)\cap A=\varnothing.
\]
The finite-DAG descent argument from the preceding lemma gives
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))\cap A=R_k.
\]
Every \(m\in\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\) lies in \(R_k=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)\cap A\).  No member of \(T_k\setminus A=O_k\) can reach \(A\), so \(m\) descends from some vertex in \(T_k\cap A\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))
\subseteq\operatorname{de}_E(T_k\cap A).
\]
Conversely, \(T_k\cap A\subseteq R_k\), and every element of the finite descendant-closed set \(R_k\) descends from a member of \(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\).  Thus the reverse inclusion holds.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)
&=\operatorname{de}_E(O_k\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))\\
&=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k\setminus A)\cup\operatorname{de}_E(T_k\cap A)\\
&=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)=F_k.
\end{aligned}
\]

Let \(Q^*=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\).  Retain \(E\), add one binary childless selection node with parent set \(\{i,j\}\) for each \(\{i,j\}\in Q^*\), and add one binary childless selection node with parent set \(\{i\}\) for every \(Q^*\)-isolated \(i\in A\).  The union of reconstructed parent sets is \(A\), its two-section is \(Q^*\), and \(B(E,A)\cup Q^*=S_0(\mathbf M)\).  Replace each nonobservational target \(T_k\) by \(T_k^*\).  The observational projection is unchanged.  The equality \(\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)=F_k\) preserves every intervention-induced path adjacency and every nonindicator endpoint, while
\[
T_k^*\cup(\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)\cap A)
=O_k\cup R_k
=Z_k(\mathbf M)
\]
preserves every indicator adjacency.  The checker characterization therefore gives equality of the fully oriented projected MAGs in every regime.

The reconstructed graph is finite and acyclic because the new selection nodes are childless.  It is causally sufficient on \(V\); every selection node is binary, childless, and observed-parented; the selected stratum, pre-treatment timing, and empty observational target are retained; and soft-intervention modularity holds for the new ordered target family.  Choose every binary selection kernel strictly between zero and one on every parent configuration.  Finiteness then gives positive probability to the joint selected stratum.  Thus \(\bar\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).

Conversely, a normalized target-residual certificate already derives its unique target family from \((\mathbf M,E,A)\).  The same pair-node and isolated-singleton construction has selection-parent union \(A\) and two-section \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\), and uses at most
\[
\lvert Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\rvert+\lvert A\rvert
\le \binom D2+D
\]
selection nodes.  When \(K=0\), \(\mathcal K_+\) is empty, so no target argument or replacement occurs.  No overlap, rank, inverse, division, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

Assume \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).  A residual-admissible pair \((E,A)\) passes
\[
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1
\]
if and only if its canonical selection reconstruction with the derived targets \(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) is a member of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Every member of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) has an equivalent passing target-residual certificate of this form, and every passing pair reconstructs a compatible member.  Consequently,
\[
\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists E,A\;
\operatorname{Check}_{D}\!\left(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M\right)=1.
\]
For \(K=0\), the certificate and equivalence contain no nonobservational target coordinate.

statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix a residual-admissible pair \((E,A)\) and its uniquely derived certificate
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)
=\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Its canonical reconstruction retains the basal DAG \(E\), uses the pair-node and isolated-singleton selection construction, sets \(I^{(0)}=\varnothing\), and sets \(I^{(k)}=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\).  By \(\texttt{lem:selection-normalization}\), the selection reconstruction has exact summary \((A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\), uses finitely many childless binary selection nodes, and satisfies the structural clauses of the full Dai class.  Choosing every reconstructed Bernoulli selection kernel strictly between zero and one gives positive probability to the finite joint selected stratum.  By \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-checker-characterization}\), the projected regime family of this reconstruction is exactly
\[
\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)).
\]

Suppose first that the canonical reconstruction belongs to \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Its regime MAG is Markov equivalent to \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K\).  Markov-equivalent MAGs have identical adjacencies and unshielded collider triples.  Hence every comparison in the checker succeeds and
\[
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1.
\]

Conversely, suppose the checker accepts.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:compatible-input}\) supplies an anchor \(\eta_0\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Therefore \(\mathcal M_{\eta_0}^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency and unshielded-collider patterns.  Acceptance supplies those same two patterns for \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\).  Both the reconstructed family and the anchor arise from one basal DAG, childless pre-treatment selection, and one ordered target family.  The cross-regime equivalence criterion in \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-checker-characterization}\) thus yields
\[
\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))
\equiv_m\mathcal M_{\eta_0}^{(k)}
\equiv_m\mathcal M^{(k)}
\qquad(k\in\mathcal K).
\]
The remaining class clauses hold by construction, so the reconstruction belongs to \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).

For exhaustiveness, take any \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Lemma \(\texttt{lem:selection-normalization}\) constructs from it a residual-admissible pair \((E,A)\) whose canonical selection-and-target reconstruction has exactly the same fully oriented projected MAG in every regime.  The forward implication just proved gives
\[
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1.
\]
Conversely, every passing pair reconstructs a compatible member by the reverse implication.  Passing target-residual certificates and compatible models therefore realize exactly the same regime-MAG families.  In particular,
\[
\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists E,A\;
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1.
\]
When \(K=0\), the nonobservational index set is empty, and the same proof uses only the observational component.  No overlap, rank, inverse, division, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every compatible oracle family \(\mathbf M\), target-residual certificate enumeration in \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\) terminates and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M).
\]
For every endpoint left circular, the retained tail and arrowhead certificates reconstruct two members of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) that agree with every fixed output mark and realize the two opposite marks at that endpoint.  Both \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) and every \(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) are uniquely computed from \((\mathbf M,E,A)\), so the algorithm visits at most
\[
3^{\binom D2}2^D
\]
pairs \((E,A)\) and admits the crude finite runtime bound
\[
O\!\left(3^{\binom D2}2^D
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
This is an exact population algorithm with a non-tight singly exponential upper bound in \(D^2\) and only polynomial dependence on \(K\) outside the search factor.  It is not a polynomial global search and not a polynomial local-rule completeness result.  For \(K=0\), no indicator-neighborhood or target-residual object is formed.
statements.justification: Endpointwise enumeration over the exact target-residual quotient is a computable semantic representative with actual opposing witnesses.
statements.gap: Dai et al. leave local CDIS completeness open; this theorem gives exact completeness by finite global search without enumerating unknown targets.
statements.consumer: The sciPlex2 A549 oracle workflow can distinguish invariant marks from certified ambiguity using paired full-class certificates.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(C=\binom D2\).  Each unordered vertex pair has at most three basal states in \(E\): absent, oriented in one direction, or oriented in the other direction.  Thus at most \(3^C\) directed graphs are visited before cyclic choices are rejected.  There are \(2^D\) subsets \(A\) before checking \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\).  Once \((E,A)\) is fixed, \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\) uniquely computes
\[
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A),
\]
and, for each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), uniquely computes
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M),\quad R_k(\mathbf M,A),\quad O_k(\mathbf M,A),
\quad T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),\quad F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A).
\]
The residual-skeleton and descendant-closure tests either reject the pair or admit that single derived certificate; they introduce no choices.  Therefore the enumeration visits at most
\[
3^C2^D=3^{\binom D2}2^D
\]
candidates and terminates.  If \(K=0\), all displayed nonobservational objects are absent and this count is unchanged.

Let
\[
\mathfrak A(\mathbf M)
=\left\{(E,A):
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1
\right\}.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:compatible-input}\) and \(\texttt{thm:finite-common-realizability}\) imply \(\mathfrak A(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).  Fix \(e=(k,u;uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\).  The two directions and exhaustiveness clause of that theorem yield
\[
\left\{
\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\bigr):
(E,A)\in\mathfrak A(\mathbf M)
\right\}
=
\left\{
\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\bigr):
\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)
\right\}.
\]
For the left-to-right inclusion, every passing pair reconstructs a compatible member.  For the reverse inclusion, target residualization of every compatible member supplies a passing pair with the same entire fully oriented regime-MAG family.

Every fully oriented MAG endpoint is a tail or an arrowhead.  Hence the common feasible set is one of
\[
\{\mathrm{tail}\},
\qquad
\{\mathrm{arrow}\},
\qquad
\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]
The output rule in \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\) returns respectively a tail, an arrowhead, or a circle, exactly as \(\texttt{def:canonical-si-pag}\) does.  The accepted certificates also have the supplied skeleton in each regime.  Consequently, endpoint by endpoint,
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M).
\]

If \(e\) is circular, its feasible set contains both marks.  The finite lexicographic enumeration therefore retains one accepted tail certificate and one accepted arrowhead certificate.  By \(\texttt{thm:finite-common-realizability}\), their canonical reconstructions are actual members of the common-basal class \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  At every fixed output endpoint the feasible set is a singleton, so both witnesses agree with every fixed mark; at \(e\) they realize opposite marks.  These are coupled whole-family witnesses, not independent regime-wise MAG completions.

For the runtime, materializing \(S_0(\mathbf M)\) and all indicator-neighborhoods costs \(O(D^2+KD)\).  For a candidate \((E,A)\), acyclicity, transitive closure, ancestor closure, all descendant closures, and all minimal-generator sets are computable in
\[
O((K+1)(D+1)^3)
\]
time.  Constructing \(B(E,A)\) checks at most \(D\) possible common children for each of \(O(D^2)\) pairs and is absorbed by the same cubic envelope.  Forming the derived residuals, constructing all regime matrices, deciding the path conditions, and comparing all unshielded triples are likewise covered by that envelope.  Updating endpointwise feasible sets and retaining the first opposing certificates costs \(O(N_{\mathrm{end}})\).  Thus the conservative per-candidate cost is
\[
O\!\left(D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right).
\]
Multiplication by the candidate count gives
\[
O\!\left(3^{\binom D2}2^D
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
The logarithm of the search factor is \(O(D^2)\); \(K\) appears only in the displayed polynomial factor.  This is a non-tight singly exponential upper bound in \(D^2\), not a polynomial algorithm.  It proves no completeness result for a fixed local orientation calculus and excludes the conditional-independence and invariance queries required to obtain the supplied oracle MAGs.  No support, overlap, rank, inverse, division, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

sampling_model.design: Population-oracle graphical input; there is no sampling randomness in the proposal kernel.
sampling_model.units: A finite observed vertex set \(V\) shared by one observational and \(K\) soft-intervention regimes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 proves soundness of oracle CDIS, while Lemmas 3--6 and Theorem 2 supply the regime-MAG formulas and equivalence substrate used to prove exact selection-and-target residualization.
Complete FCI orients every invariant endpoint in one ordinary MAG equivalence class.
The unknown-target soft-intervention completeness theory excludes selection bias.
The paper studies orientation completeness with background knowledge inside restricted MAG settings.
Theorem 4 gives F-FCI completeness under post-treatment selection and different F-PAG semantics.

tldr: Selective enrollment precedes intervention in many perturbation studies, so one indicator-free observational MAG on \(V\) and the nonobservational MAGs on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) are coupled projections of one unobserved basal-world DAG rather than independent equivalence classes. The project defines the canonical SI-PAG as endpoint-mark invariance over Dai et al.'s full causally sufficient compatibility class and isolates the open construction of a finite sound within- and cross-regime calculus with globally compatible opposing witnesses for every residual circle. Resolving that extension problem yields mark completeness and complete population CDIS, with a finite matrix input, a cost for matching each rule, and a polynomial total orientation-closure certificate, while making no polynomial claim for conditional-independence discovery.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize pre-treatment-selection interventional equivalence and prove oracle CDIS soundness, but explicitly leave both a graphical representative of the equivalence class and CDIS completeness open.
project_justification.niche: Ordinary FCI completeness treats one MAG class, and \(\Psi\)-FCI completeness treats unknown soft targets without the basal selection world; neither supplies paired realizations that preserve all of Dai's cross-regime twin constraints.
project_justification.fill: The project isolates a twin-compatible extension lemma, uses it to equate finitely encoded monotone rule closure with semantic endpoint invariance, and packages the result as complete population discovery with an explicit per-rule and total oracle-input orientation cost.

related_work: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention supplies the published twin-graph semantics coupling an indicator-free observational regime to indicator-bearing nonobservational regimes, the adjacency-and-v-structure equivalence theorem, the two-variable selection-versus-causation witness, and a sound but not complete CDIS procedure. Zhang2008CompleteFCI supplies the discriminating-path and circle-component proof architecture for a single observational MAG class. JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020 supplies an augmented intervention-MAG realizability lemma and paired endpoint witnesses for unknown soft targets, but its tail-completeness argument explicitly excludes selection bias. AliRichardsonSpirtes2009 supplies the ordered-collider equivalence criterion that explains why ordinary MAG reasoning must be checked before exploiting Dai's special reduction. VenkateswaranPerkovic2026 and WangDuZhou2025 show that generic background-knowledge closure requires additional dense-graph rules and remains distinct from globally coupled twin realizability. LuoEtAl2026PostTreatmentSelection gives a complete F-PAG for selection after intervention, whose square marks and inducing-node semantics do not represent Dai's basal selection. ColomboMaathuisKalischRichardson2012 is relevant only to a later finite-sample rung; the present kernel begins with finitely encoded oracle regime MAGs and bounds only their orientation closure.
technical_internal_limitation: Independent within-regime MAG completions are not accepted as compatibility witnesses: every completion used by the calculus must be realized by one basal DAG and one ordered unknown-target family. A generic non-two-variable finite obstruction family and its calculus certificate remain open diagnostics rather than theorem contributions in this core.
honest_scope: The theorem-level target is population mark completeness on Dai et al.'s published causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection class, with regime zero projected on \(V\) without an intervention indicator and each regime in \(\mathcal K_+\) projected on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The finite rule construction and globally compatible paired-witness lemma are open. The stated polynomial certificate covers matrix initialization and orientation-rule closure from supplied oracle MAGs; finite-sample consistency, latent common causes, post-treatment filtering, effect identification, and the number of conditional-independence or invariance queries used to discover those MAGs are outside the claim. In the no-intervention, no-selection special case, the construction must collapse to the ordinary CPDAG.
